roleplay.title: Doña Carmen's childhood
roleplay.setup: You are chatting with Doña Carmen, your elderly neighbor, on her front porch. Ask her about her childhood in Mexico and how she came to Chicago. Use usted.
roleplay.persona: You are Doña Carmen, 78, born in a small town (un pueblo) in Jalisco, Mexico. The learner is your younger neighbor; you call him 'mijo' and use tú with him, but he should use usted with you. Background: you grew up on a small ranch with seven brothers and sisters; your father grew corn and beans; every morning you carried water from the well and helped your mother make tortillas; you walked 30 minutes to the elementary school; on Sundays the whole family went to Mass and then to the plaza. You met your husband, Rogelio, at a town fiesta when you were 18; you married at 20; you came to Chicago in 1972 because Rogelio found work in a steel mill; it was January and it was the first time you saw snow (say it as 'era la primera vez que veía la nieve'). Speak at an intermediate level, mixing the imperfect (for habits and descriptions) and the preterite (for events). Keep sentences short and clear. Avoid the subjunctive and the pluperfect (había + participle). Reveal details only when the learner asks; react warmly to questions.
roleplay.opening: Ay, mijo, cuando yo era niña, la vida era muy diferente.
goals: Find out where she lived as a child and what her house was like
Ask what she used to do every day as a child
Find out how she met her husband
Ask when and why she came to Chicago and what it was like when she arrived

roleplay.title: The night everything went wrong
roleplay.setup: Your friend Gabriela had a crazy night on Friday. Get the whole story: set the scene, what happened, and how it ended. Use tú.
roleplay.persona: You are Gabriela, 32, from Tegucigalpa, Honduras, a friend of the learner; use tú. The story: on Friday night it was raining and very cold; you were at home alone making dinner and watching TV; it was about nine o'clock when suddenly the power went out (se fue la luz); you looked for a flashlight but couldn't find it (no pude encontrarla); you tried to call your sister but your phone had very little battery and it died; then you heard a noise at the door and you were very scared; it was your neighbor, Don Luis, with candles; you found out the next day that a tree fell on a power line. Use the imperfect for the scene (llovía, hacía frío, estaba sola, eran las nueve) and the preterite for events. Keep language intermediate, with short sentences. Avoid the subjunctive and the pluperfect. Tell the story only bit by bit, as the learner asks questions.
roleplay.opening: ¡No sabes lo que me pasó el viernes en la noche!
goals: Ask what the weather was like and what she was doing at home
Find out what time it was when the power went out
Find out whether she managed to call anyone
Ask who was at the door and how she found out why the power went out

title: Plans and recent past
goal: Talk about your plans, what you have (or haven't) done lately, and how long you've been doing something.

grammar.h: ir a + infinitive: the everyday future
grammar.p: To talk about plans, use *ir* (voy, vas, va, vamos, van) + *a* + infinitive. In conversation this is the normal way to talk about the future. Time words like *mañana*, *esta noche*, *el sábado*, *la próxima semana* go at the start or the end.
ex: Voy a llamar a mi mamá esta noche.
I'm going to call my mom tonight.
¿Qué vas a hacer el sábado?
What are you going to do on Saturday?
Mañana va a llover.
It's going to rain tomorrow.

grammar.h: Simple future, and guessing about now
grammar.p: Add *-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án* to the whole infinitive: *viajaré, comerás, vivirá, iremos, estarán*. Common irregular stems: *tendr-* (tener), *podr-* (poder), *saldr-* (salir), *vendr-* (venir), *pondr-* (poner), *har-* (hacer), *dir-* (decir), *sabr-* (saber), *querr-* (querer). It sounds a bit more formal or certain than *ir a*. In everyday speech it is also used to GUESS about the present: *¿Dónde estará?* = I wonder where he is. *Serán las tres.* = It's probably about three.
ex: El próximo año viajaremos a México.
Next year we will travel to Mexico.
Mañana no tendré tiempo.
Tomorrow I won't have time.
Juan no contesta. Estará ocupado.
Juan isn't answering. He's probably busy.

grammar.h: Present perfect: ever, never, yet, lately
grammar.p: *he, has, ha, hemos, han* + participle (*-ar* → *-ado*, *-er/-ir* → *-ido*): *he trabajado, has comido, ha vivido*. Irregular participles: *hecho* (hacer), *dicho* (decir), *visto* (ver), *escrito* (escribir), *puesto* (poner), *vuelto* (volver), *abierto* (abrir), *roto* (romper). Use it with *alguna vez* (ever), *nunca* (never), *ya* (already/yet), *todavía no* (not yet), *últimamente* (lately). For a finished event at a stated time (*ayer, anoche, el lunes*) keep using the preterite. Note: in Mexico you will also hear the preterite with *ya* (*¿Ya comiste?*), which is correct too; in this level's exercises the hint or the options tell you which form is wanted.
ex: ¿Alguna vez has ido a Oaxaca?
Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
Todavía no he hecho la tarea.
I haven't done the homework yet.
Últimamente he dormido mal.
Lately I've been sleeping badly.

grammar.p: Present tense of *acabar* (acabo, acabas, acaba, acabamos, acaban) + *de* + infinitive = to have just done something. Keep *acabar* in the present for this meaning.
ex: Acabo de llegar.
I just arrived.
Mis padres acaban de comer.
My parents just ate.

grammar.h: How long: desde hace, hace … que, llevar
grammar.p: Spanish uses the PRESENT tense for something that started in the past and is still going on. Three common patterns: (1) present + *desde hace* + time; (2) *Hace* + time + *que* + present; (3) *llevar* + time (+ place, or + *-ando/-iendo* form: *trabajando, viviendo, esperando*). To ask: *¿Desde cuándo…?*, *¿Cuánto tiempo hace que…?*, *¿Cuánto tiempo llevas…?*
ex: Vivo en Chicago desde hace diez años.
I've lived in Chicago for ten years.
Hace tres meses que estudio español.
I've been studying Spanish for three months.
Llevo dos horas esperando.
I've been waiting for two hours.
¿Cuánto tiempo llevas en este trabajo?
How long have you been at this job?

vocab: to have been (for a period of time)
to visit (a place) for the first time
to have a birthday, to turn (an age)
phrases: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
What are you going to do this weekend?
A lo mejor voy al cine.
Maybe I'll go to the movies.
Have you ever been to Mexico?
What have you been up to lately?
How long have you been here?
How long have you lived in Chicago?
Hace tres años que trabajo aquí.
I've been working here for three years.
Ha sido una semana muy larga.
It's been a very long week.

items.q: Mañana yo ___ a visitar a mis padres.
items.qen: Tomorrow I'm going to visit my parents.
items.why: A plan for tomorrow → ir a + infinitive. Yo → voy.

items.q: ¿Qué ___ a hacer ustedes el sábado?
items.qen: What are you all going to do on Saturday?
items.why: Ustedes takes the ellos form: van a hacer.

items.q: El próximo año mi esposa y yo ___ a España.
items.qen: Next year my wife and I will travel to Spain.
items.why: 'Mi esposa y yo' = nosotros; future → viajaremos.

items.q: Mañana no ___ tiempo para comer.
items.qen: Tomorrow I won't have time to eat.
items.why: Tener has the irregular future stem tendr- → tendré.

items.q: Your friend is late and not answering. You wonder aloud: 'Where could she be?' Which is natural?
items.why: The simple future expresses a guess about the present: ¿Dónde estará? = I wonder where she is.

items.q: Someone asks you the time. You have no watch. Which reply expresses a guess ('It's probably about three')?
items.why: Future of probability: Serán las tres = it's probably three. 'Son las tres' states it as a fact.

items.q: Nosotros ya ___ comido.
items.qen: We have already eaten.
items.why: Haber for nosotros in the present perfect is hemos.

items.q: ¿Has ___ la nueva película?
items.qen: Have you seen the new movie?
items.why: Ver has the irregular participle visto.

items.q: Todavía no he ___ el informe.
items.qen: I haven't written the report yet.
items.why: Escribir has the irregular participle escrito.

items.q: To a friend: «¿Alguna vez ___ a Oaxaca?»
items.qen: Have you ever been to Oaxaca?
items.why: Tú + present perfect → has ido. 'He ido' is 'I have', 'han ido' is 'they / you all have'.

items.q: How do you say 'I just got home'?
items.why: 'Just did' = acabar in the PRESENT + de + infinitive: Acabo de llegar.

items.q: Vivo en Chicago ___ diez años.
items.qen: I've lived in Chicago for ten years.
items.why: An ongoing situation with the present tense → desde hace + time.

items.q: ___ dos años que trabajo en este hospital.
items.qen: I've been working at this hospital for two years.
items.why: Pattern: Hace + time + que + present.

items.q: How do you say 'I've been in this country for fifteen years'?
opts: Soy quince años en este país.
Llevo quince años en este país.
Llevo en este país desde quince años.
Voy quince años en este país.
items.why: Llevar + time (+ place): Llevo quince años en este país.

items.q: How do you ask a coworker 'How long have you been working here?'
items.why: Still working there → llevar in the present: ¿Cuánto tiempo llevas trabajando aquí? 'Trabajaste' means the job is over.

items.q: Últimamente ___ muy cansado.
items.qen: Lately I've been very tired.
items.why: 'Lately' → present perfect: he estado (participle of estar = estado).

items.q: A friend asks: «¿Ya has comido?» You haven't eaten yet. Best reply?
opts: Todavía no. Voy a comer en un rato.
Todavía no. Comí en un rato.
items.why: Not yet → Todavía no; the plan to eat soon → voy a comer.

items.q: Mañana mis hijos ___ a las seis.
items.qen: Tomorrow my kids will come at six.
items.why: Mañana → future. Venir has the irregular future stem vendr-; ellos → vendrán.

items.q: ¿Qué ___ tú en las próximas vacaciones?
items.qen: What will you do on your next vacation?
items.why: Hacer has the irregular future stem har-; tú → harás.

items.q: Mi hermano todavía no ha ___ de su viaje.
items.qen: My brother hasn't come back from his trip yet.
items.why: Volver has the irregular participle vuelto.

items.q: Esta noche ___ a cenar con mis amigos.
items.en: Tonight I'm going to have dinner with my friends.
items.why: ir a + infinitive; yo → voy.

items.q: ¿Qué ___ a hacer tú después del trabajo?
items.en: What are you going to do after work?
items.why: Tú → vas a hacer.

items.q: Mañana ___ a llover.
items.en: It's going to rain tomorrow.
items.why: Weather uses the él form: va a llover.

items.q: El sábado nosotros ___ una fiesta.
items.en: On Saturday we're going to have a party.
items.why: Nosotros → vamos a hacer.

items.q: El año que viene ___ a Guatemala.
items.en: Next year I will travel to Guatemala.
items.why: Infinitive + -é → viajaré.

items.q: Mi hija ___ diez años en mayo.
items.en: My daughter will be ten in May.
items.why: Tener → irregular stem tendr- + á → tendrá.

items.q: Juan no contesta el teléfono. ___ ocupado.
items.en: Juan isn't answering the phone. He's probably busy.
items.why: A guess about the present → simple future: estará.

items.q: —¿Qué hora ___? —No sé, serán las cinco.
items.en: —I wonder what time it is. —I don't know, it's probably five.
items.why: Wondering about the present → simple future: ¿Qué hora será?

items.q: ¿___ comido ya?
items.en: Have you eaten yet? (to a friend)
items.why: Tú form of haber → has.

items.q: Mis padres nunca ___ en avión.
items.en: My parents have never traveled by plane.
items.why: Ellos → han + viajado.

items.q: Todavía no ___ la tarea.
items.en: I haven't done the homework yet.
items.why: Hacer has the irregular participle hecho → he hecho.

items.q: Ella nunca ___ eso.
items.en: She has never said that.
items.why: Decir has the irregular participle dicho → ha dicho.

items.q: Señora, ¿alguna vez ___ el mole poblano?
items.en: Ma'am, have you ever tried mole poblano?
items.why: Usted → ha + probado.

items.q: ¿Ya ___ las ventanas?
items.en: Have you all opened the windows yet?
items.why: Abrir has the irregular participle abierto → han abierto.

items.q: Últimamente mi papá no ___ bien.
items.en: Lately my dad hasn't been sleeping well.
items.why: Últimamente → present perfect: ha dormido.

items.q: Acabo ___ hablar con mi jefe.
items.en: I just talked with my boss.
items.why: acabar de + infinitive.

items.q: Mi esposa ___ de salir.
items.en: My wife just left.
items.why: 'Just did' keeps acabar in the present: acaba de salir.

items.q: Vivimos en este barrio ___ hace cinco años.
items.en: We've lived in this neighborhood for five years.
items.why: Present + desde hace + time.

items.q: ___ tres meses que estudio español.
items.en: I've been studying Spanish for three months.
items.why: Hace + time + que + present.

items.q: ¿Cuánto tiempo ___ esperando, señora?
items.en: How long have you been waiting, ma'am?
items.why: Usted → lleva + time/gerund.

items.en: I'm going to call my mom tonight.
items.a: Voy a llamar a mi mamá esta noche.
alt: Esta noche voy a llamar a mi mamá.
Voy a llamar esta noche a mi mamá.

items.en: What are you going to do this weekend? (to a friend)
items.a: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
alt: ¿Este fin de semana qué vas a hacer?

items.en: We will travel to Mexico next year.
items.a: Viajaremos a México el próximo año.
alt: El próximo año viajaremos a México.
Viajaremos el próximo año a México.

items.en: Have you ever been to Guatemala? (to a friend)
items.a: ¿Alguna vez has ido a Guatemala?
alt: ¿Has ido alguna vez a Guatemala?
¿Has ido a Guatemala alguna vez?

items.en: I haven't finished the report yet.
items.a: Todavía no he terminado el informe.
alt: No he terminado el informe todavía.
No he terminado todavía el informe.

items.en: We have never seen that movie.
items.a: Nunca hemos visto esa película.

items.en: I just arrived at the hospital.
items.a: Acabo de llegar al hospital.

items.en: My parents just ate.
items.a: Mis padres acaban de comer.
alt: Acaban de comer mis padres.

items.en: I've lived in Chicago for ten years.
items.a: Vivo en Chicago desde hace diez años.
alt: Desde hace diez años vivo en Chicago.
Vivo desde hace diez años en Chicago.

items.en: I've been studying Spanish for two years.
items.a: Hace dos años que estudio español.

items.en: How long have you been in the United States, sir?
items.a: ¿Cuánto tiempo lleva en Estados Unidos, señor?
alt: Señor, ¿cuánto tiempo lleva en Estados Unidos?

items.en: It's probably ten at night.
items.a: Serán las diez de la noche.

items.en: I wonder where Ana is at this hour.
items.a: ¿Dónde estará Ana a esta hora?
alt: ¿A esta hora dónde estará Ana?

items.en: Tomorrow I'm not going to have time.
items.a: Mañana no voy a tener tiempo.
alt: No voy a tener tiempo mañana.

items.en: What have you been up to lately? (to a friend)
items.a: ¿Qué has hecho últimamente?
alt: ¿Últimamente qué has hecho?

items.en: My sister is going to have a baby in June.
items.a: Mi hermana va a tener un bebé en junio.
alt: En junio mi hermana va a tener un bebé.
Mi hermana en junio va a tener un bebé.

items.say: Voy a llamar a mi hermano mañana.
opts: I'm going to call my brother tomorrow.
My brother is going to call me tomorrow.

items.say: Ya hemos comido.
Todavía no he visto a mi médico.
opts: My doctor hasn't seen me yet.
I haven't seen my doctor yet.
I'm going to see my doctor.

items.say: Acaban de llegar del aeropuerto.
opts: They're about to leave for the airport.
They just arrived from the airport.
We just arrived at the airport.
They're going to arrive at the airport.

items.say: Llevo seis meses en este trabajo.
opts: I worked at this job for six months.
I'm going to start this job in six months.
I left this job six months ago.
I've been at this job for six months.

items.say: ¿Dónde estará mi celular?
opts: Where is my cell phone going to be?
Where did I leave my cell phone?
I wonder where my cell phone is.

items.say: Hace dos semanas que no duermo bien.
opts: I haven't slept well for two weeks.
I slept well two weeks ago.
I'm going to sleep better in two weeks.
I didn't sleep well two weeks ago.

items.say: ¿Alguna vez ha estado en el hospital?
opts: Were you in the hospital yesterday?
Have you ever been in the hospital?
Are you going to the hospital?
Has he always been at the hospital?

items.say: El sábado vamos a ir a la playa.
opts: On Saturday we went to the beach.
On Saturday we're going to go to the beach.
On Saturdays we go to the beach.
On Saturday they're going to the beach.

items.say: Mis hijos volverán el domingo.
opts: My kids came back on Sunday.
My kids come back on Sundays.
My kids want to come back on Sunday.
My kids will come back on Sunday.

turns.es: Oye, ¿qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
turns.en: Hey, what are you going to do this weekend?

opts: Voy a descansar y ver un partido.
Fui a descansar y vi un partido.
Vas a descansar y ver un partido.
turns.why: He asks about plans → ir a + infinitive, yo form: voy a descansar.

turns.es: ¡Qué bien! ¿Ya has ido al nuevo restaurante mexicano de la esquina?
turns.en: Nice! Have you been to the new Mexican restaurant on the corner yet?

opts: Todavía no, pero voy a ir el domingo.
Todavía no, pero fui el domingo.
turns.why: Not yet → todavía no; a future plan → voy a ir. 'Fui el domingo' contradicts 'todavía no'.

turns.es: Te va a encantar. Los tacos son buenísimos.
turns.en: You're going to love it. The tacos are amazing.

turns.es: ¿Dónde estás? Ya son las ocho.
turns.en: Where are you? It's already eight.

opts: Lo siento, saldré de casa ayer.
Lo siento, acabo de salir de casa.
Lo siento, he salido de casa mañana.
turns.why: 'I just left' → acabo de salir. The other two mix tense and time word (future + ayer, perfect + mañana).

turns.es: Bueno. ¿Cuánto vas a tardar?
turns.en: Okay. How long are you going to take?

turns.why: She asks about the future → llegaré en unos veinte minutos. 'Tardé' is past; 'Llevo' means 'I've been (for) twenty minutes'.

turns.es: Está bien. Aquí te espero.
turns.en: Okay. I'll wait for you here.

turns.es: Buenas tardes. Usted es nuevo en el edificio, ¿verdad?
turns.en: Good afternoon. You're new in the building, right?

opts: Sí, llevo aquí desde una semana.
turns.why: Llevar + time + place, present tense: llevo una semana aquí.

turns.es: Bienvenido. Yo vivo aquí desde hace treinta años. ¿Va a vivir aquí mucho tiempo?
turns.en: Welcome. I've lived here for thirty years. Are you going to live here a long time?

opts: Sí, viví aquí por lo menos dos años.
Sí, voy a vivir aquí por lo menos dos años.
Sí, vas a vivir aquí por lo menos dos años.
turns.why: A plan → voy a vivir. 'Viví' is past; 'vas' is the wrong person.

turns.es: Qué bueno. ¿Y ya ha conocido a los otros vecinos?
turns.en: Good. And have you met the other neighbors yet?

opts: Solo he conocido a la señora del segundo piso.
Solo has conocido a la señora del segundo piso.
Solo conoceré a la señora del segundo piso ayer.
turns.why: Answering about yourself → he conocido. 'Has' is tú; 'conoceré … ayer' mixes future with a past time word.

turns.es: Ah, doña Carmen. Es muy amable. Si necesita algo, aquí estoy.
turns.en: Ah, Doña Carmen. She's very kind. If you need anything, I'm here.

items.title: Catching up with an old friend

turns.es: ¡Cuánto tiempo! ¿Qué has hecho últimamente?
turns.en: Long time no see! What have you been up to lately?

opts: Trabajaré mucho y viajaba un poco.
He trabajado mucho y he viajado un poco.
Ha trabajado mucho y ha viajado un poco.
turns.why: She asks with the present perfect about yourself → he trabajado, he viajado. 'Ha' would be he/she.

turns.es: ¿Sabes qué? Mi esposo y yo vamos a tener un bebé.
turns.en: Guess what? My husband and I are going to have a baby.

turns.why: The baby hasn't been born yet → ¿Cuándo va a nacer?

turns.es: En marzo. ¡Estamos muy contentos!
turns.en: In March. We're very happy!

items.title: Small talk at a hospital party

turns.es: ¿Desde cuándo trabajas en el hospital?
turns.en: How long have you been working at the hospital?

opts: Trabajo aquí desde hace un año.
Trabajé aquí desde hace un año.
Trabajo aquí hace desde un año.
turns.why: Still working there → present + desde hace: Trabajo aquí desde hace un año.

turns.es: ¿Y vivías en Chicago antes?
turns.en: And did you live in Chicago before?

opts: No, llevaré un año en Chicago.
No, llevo en Chicago desde un año.
No, llevo un año en Chicago.
turns.why: Llevar (present) + time + place: llevo un año en Chicago.

turns.es: ¡Bienvenido! ¿Ya has probado la pizza de Chicago?
turns.en: Welcome! Have you tried Chicago pizza yet?

opts: Todavía no, pero el sábado he ido a una pizzería.
Todavía no, pero el sábado voy a ir a una pizzería.
Todavía no, pero el sábado fui a una pizzería.
turns.why: Not yet + a plan → voy a ir. The other two say you already went, which contradicts 'todavía no'.

turns.es: ¡Ya me contarás qué tal!
turns.en: Let me know how it is!

turns.es: Papá, ¿por qué no ha llegado el abuelo?
turns.en: Dad, why hasn't Grandpa arrived?

opts: No sé. Estará en el tráfico.
No sé. Estuvo en el tráfico mañana.
No sé. Estarás en el tráfico.
turns.why: A guess about the present → future of probability, él form: estará.

turns.es: ¿Y qué hora es?
turns.en: And what time is it?

opts: No sé, eran como las seis mañana.
No sé, serás como las seis.
No sé, serán como las seis.
turns.why: Guessing the time → serán (plural, agreeing with 'las seis').

turns.es: ¡Ah, mira! Acaba de llegar.
turns.en: Oh, look! He just got here.

roleplay.title: Weekend plans in the break room
roleplay.setup: It's Friday afternoon. You're chatting with Gabriela, a nurse you work with, about plans for the weekend and what you've both been up to lately.
roleplay.persona: You play Gabriela, 34, a nurse originally from Guadalajara, Mexico, who has lived in Chicago for 8 years and has worked at this hospital for 3 years. Friendly, chatty, uses tú. Use short, clear sentences built around this level's grammar: ir a + infinitive, the simple future (including guesses like 'estará cansado'), the present perfect (ya, todavía no, alguna vez, nunca, últimamente), acabar de, and desde hace / hace … que / llevar. Avoid the subjunctive. Facts to reveal only when asked: she just got back from visiting her family in Guadalajara (acaba de regresar); on Sunday she is going to run a 10K race; she has never been to a baseball game at Wrigley Field; lately she has been studying for a nursing certification exam and has slept little. Ask the learner about his plans and whether he has ever been to Guadalajara. If he makes a tense error, react naturally (e.g., '¿Ah, ya fuiste? ¿O vas a ir?') rather than correcting formally.
roleplay.opening: ¡Hola! ¡Por fin es viernes! ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?
goals: Tell her at least two things you are going to do this weekend
Find out what she is going to do on Sunday
Ask how long she has lived in Chicago
Ask whether she has ever been to a baseball game
Ask what she has been doing lately

roleplay.title: Meeting an older neighbor
roleplay.setup: You meet Don Ernesto, an older man who lives on your floor, in the elevator. Use usted. Get to know him: how long he has lived there and what his plans are.
roleplay.persona: You play Don Ernesto, 72, a retired baker from Michoacán, Mexico. Polite and warm; use usted with the learner and expect usted back. Speak slowly with simple sentences using this level's grammar: ir a + infinitive, simple future, present perfect, acabar de, desde hace / hace … que / llevar. Avoid the subjunctive. Facts to reveal only when asked: he has lived in the building for 25 years (desde hace veinticinco años); his granddaughter was just born last week (acaba de nacer su nieta); in December he is going to travel to Michoacán by bus because he has never flown on a plane; lately he has been walking every morning in the park. Ask the learner how long he has been in the building and whether he has ever visited Michoacán.
roleplay.opening: Buenas tardes. Usted acaba de llegar al edificio, ¿verdad?
goals: Introduce yourself and say how long you've been living in the building
Ask him how long he has lived there, using usted
Find out his plans for December
Ask whether he has ever traveled by plane
Find out what he has been doing lately

title: Pronouns and ongoing actions
goal: Replace nouns with pronouns, describe your daily routine, and say what you (and others) are doing right now.

grammar.p: Direct object (WHAT or WHOM): *me, te, lo, la, nos, los, las*. Use *lo/la/los/las* for things and people, matching gender and number: *el celular → lo*, *las llaves → las*. Indirect object (TO/FOR whom): *me, te, le, nos, les*, with verbs like *dar, decir, mandar, prestar, explicar, preguntar, pedir*. The pronoun goes BEFORE a conjugated verb. Spanish often keeps the indirect pronoun even when the person is named: *Le di el regalo a mi mamá.* In Latin America, use *lo/la* (not *le*) for 'him/her' as a direct object: *Lo vi ayer.*
ex: ¿El celular? No lo encuentro.
The cell phone? I can't find it.
Las llaves las tengo yo.
I've got the keys.
Mi hermano me mandó un mensaje.
My brother sent me a message.
Le expliqué el problema a mi jefe.
I explained the problem to my boss.

grammar.h: Two pronouns together: se lo, me la, te los
grammar.p: When you use both, the indirect (person) comes first, then the direct (thing): *me lo, te la, nos los*. If both start with *l*, *le* or *les* changes to *se*: never *le lo*, always *se lo*. *Se* can mean to him, to her, to you (usted), to them, or to you all; add *a él / a ella / a usted* if you need to be clear.
ex: ¿Me prestas tu carro? —Sí, te lo presto.
Will you lend me your car? —Yes, I'll lend it to you.
¿Le diste el libro a Pedro? —Sí, se lo di.
Did you give the book to Pedro? —Yes, I gave it to him.
Las fotos se las mandé a mis papás.
I sent the photos to my parents.

grammar.h: Reflexive verbs and the daily routine
grammar.p: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: *me, te, se, nos, se*. *Levantarse*: *me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, se levantan*. Many routine verbs work this way: *despertarse (me despierto), acostarse (me acuesto), vestirse (me visto), bañarse, lavarse los dientes, sentirse (me siento)*. With body parts and clothes, Spanish uses *el/la*, not 'my': *Me lavo las manos.* Compare: *Me despierto* (I wake up) vs. *Mi mamá me despierta* (My mom wakes me up). In Mexico, *bañarse* is the everyday word for taking a shower.
ex: Me levanto a las seis y me baño.
I get up at six and take a shower.
Los niños se acuestan a las nueve.
The kids go to bed at nine.
¿Cómo te sientes hoy?
How are you feeling today?

grammar.h: Right now and still: estar + gerund, seguir + gerund
grammar.p: For an action in progress right now: *estar* + gerund. Gerunds: *-ar → -ando* (trabajando), *-er/-ir → -iendo* (comiendo, viviendo). Spelling and stem changes: *leyendo, oyendo, trayendo, durmiendo, diciendo, pidiendo, sintiendo, viniendo*. For 'still / keep on doing': *seguir* + gerund (*sigo, sigues, sigue, seguimos, siguen*): *Sigue lloviendo* = It's still raining.
ex: Estoy manejando, te llamo después.
I'm driving, I'll call you later.
El bebé está durmiendo.
The baby is sleeping.
Mi papá sigue trabajando a los setenta años.
My dad is still working at seventy.

grammar.p: Before a conjugated verb: *Lo veo.* With an infinitive or a gerund you have TWO correct choices: before the conjugated verb, or attached to the end: *Lo voy a llamar = Voy a llamarlo*; *Me estoy vistiendo = Estoy vistiéndome*. Never in the middle (*voy a lo llamar* is wrong). With an affirmative command the pronoun must be attached: *Dime. Dámelo. Dígame.* When attaching adds syllables, write an accent to keep the stress where it was: *haciendo → haciéndolo*, *da → dámelo*. Attaching ONE pronoun to an infinitive needs no accent (*llamarlo, verte*), but two pronouns do (*devolvértelo*).
ex: Te voy a llamar mañana. / Voy a llamarte mañana.
I'm going to call you tomorrow.
Lo estoy haciendo. / Estoy haciéndolo.
I'm doing it.
¿Tu libro? Te lo quiero devolver. / Quiero devolvértelo.
Your book? I want to give it back to you.
Dime la verdad.
Tell me the truth.

vocab: right now / in a little bit (Mexico)
phrases: I'm driving, I'll call you later.
Will you lend it to me?
I'll give it back to you tomorrow.
Tell me. / How can I help you? (usted)
What time do you go to bed?

items.q: ¿Dónde está mi celular? No ___ veo.
items.qen: Where's my cell phone? I don't see it.
items.why: El celular is masculine singular → lo.

items.q: ¿Tienes las llaves? —Sí, ___ tengo aquí.
items.qen: Do you have the keys? —Yes, I have them here.
items.why: Las llaves is feminine plural → las.

items.q: ¿Compraste la leche? —Sí, ___ compré esta mañana.
items.qen: Did you buy the milk? —Yes, I bought it this morning.
items.why: La leche is feminine singular → la.

items.q: Ayer ___ di un regalo a mi mamá.
items.qen: Yesterday I gave my mom a gift.
items.why: To my mom = indirect object → le. 'Se' only replaces le when another pronoun (lo/la) follows.

items.q: Mis hijos siempre ___ piden dinero.
items.qen: My kids always ask me for money.
items.why: 'Ask me' → indirect object pronoun me, placed before the verb.

items.q: ¿Le diste el libro a Pedro? —Sí, ya ___ di.
items.qen: Did you give the book to Pedro? —Yes, I already gave it to him.
items.why: Le + lo → se lo (le becomes se before lo). El libro is masculine → lo.

items.q: ¿Me prestas tu pluma? —Sí, ___ presto.
items.qen: Will you lend me your pen? —Yes, I'll lend it to you.
items.why: To you (tú) = te; la pluma is feminine = la → te la.

items.q: ¿Les mandaste las fotos a tus papás? —Sí, ___ mandé anoche.
items.qen: Did you send the photos to your parents? —Yes, I sent them to them last night.
items.why: Les + las → se las. Las fotos is feminine plural.

items.q: Todos los días ___ levanto a las seis.
items.qen: Every day I get up at six.
items.why: Reflexive pronoun matches the subject: yo → me levanto.

items.q: Los niños ___ acuestan a las nueve.
items.qen: The kids go to bed at nine.
items.why: Ellos → reflexive se: se acuestan.

items.q: En este momento mi esposa ___.
items.qen: My wife is taking a shower right now.
items.why: In progress right now → estar + gerund, and bañarse needs se: se está bañando. 'Está bañando' without se means she is bathing someone else.

items.q: El bebé está ___.
items.qen: The baby is sleeping.
items.why: Dormir changes o → u in the gerund: durmiendo.

items.q: ¿Qué estás ___?
items.qen: What are you reading?
items.why: Leer → leyendo (the i becomes y between vowels).

items.q: Mi papá ___ trabajando a los setenta años.
items.qen: My dad is still working at seventy.
items.why: Seguir + gerund = still doing. Él → sigue (with u to keep the hard g sound).

items.q: How do you say 'I'm going to call him tomorrow'?
items.why: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb (Lo voy a llamar) or attached to the infinitive (voy a llamarlo) — never in the middle or as a separate word after the infinitive.

items.q: Which is spelled correctly? ('I'm doing it.')
items.why: Attaching lo adds a syllable, so the stress (on -cien-) is now third from the end and needs a written accent: haciéndolo.

items.q: Your friend is holding your phone. Tell him: 'Give it to me.'
items.why: Affirmative command: pronouns are attached, indirect before direct, with an accent: dámelo.

items.q: How do you say 'I feel tired'?
items.why: Sentirse is reflexive and stem-changing (e → ie): me siento.

items.q: ¿La receta? Mi mamá ___ va a mandar mañana.
items.qen: The recipe? My mom is going to send it to me tomorrow.
items.why: To me = me, la receta = la; indirect first → me la.

items.q: Disculpe, señor, ¿___ puedo hacer una pregunta?
items.qen: Excuse me, sir, may I ask you a question?
items.why: Hacer una pregunta A usted → indirect object le.

items.q: ¿Viste a Carlos? —Sí, ___ vi en el gimnasio.
items.en: Did you see Carlos? —Yes, I saw him at the gym.
items.why: Carlos is the direct object, masculine → lo (standard in Latin America).

items.q: ¿Dónde pusiste las tazas? —___ puse en la mesa.
items.en: Where did you put the cups? —I put them on the table.
items.why: Las tazas is feminine plural → las.

items.q: Mi hermano ___ escribió una carta a mi abuela.
items.en: My brother wrote a letter to my grandmother.
items.why: A mi abuela is the indirect object → le (Spanish keeps le even when the person is named).

items.q: ¿Me ayudas? —Claro, ___ ayudo.
items.en: Will you help me? —Sure, I'll help you.
items.why: You (tú) as an object → te.

items.q: ¿Les explicaste el plan a los niños? —Sí, ya ___ expliqué.
items.en: Did you explain the plan to the kids? —Yes, I already explained it to them.
items.why: Les + lo → se lo. El plan is masculine singular.

items.q: Necesito tu carro mañana. ¿___ prestas?
items.en: I need your car tomorrow. Will you lend it to me?
items.why: To me = me, el carro = lo → me lo.

items.q: Todos los días ___ despierto a las cinco y media.
items.en: Every day I wake up at five thirty.
items.why: Despertarse, yo → me despierto.

items.q: Mis hijos ___ los dientes después de comer.
items.en: My kids brush their teeth after eating.
items.why: Ellos → se lavan. Spanish uses los dientes, not 'their teeth'.

items.q: Anoche ___ muy tarde.
items.en: Last night I went to bed very late.
items.why: Anoche → preterite; yo → me acosté (no stem change in the preterite).

items.q: ¿A qué hora ___ tú normalmente?
items.en: What time do you usually get up?
items.why: Tú → te levantas.

items.q: No puedo hablar ahora, ___ manejando.
items.en: I can't talk now, I'm driving.
items.why: In progress → estar + gerund; yo → estoy.

items.q: Los niños están ___ en el parque.
items.en: The kids are playing in the park.
items.why: -ar verb → -ando: jugando.

items.q: Mi abuela está ___ el periódico.
items.en: My grandmother is reading the newspaper.
items.why: Leer → leyendo.

items.q: Perdón, ¿qué me estás ___?
items.en: Sorry, what are you telling me?
items.why: Decir has the gerund diciendo (e → i).

items.q: Mi mamá ___ trabajando en la misma tienda.
items.en: My mom is still working at the same store.
items.why: Seguir + gerund = still doing; ella → sigue.

items.q: Nosotros ___ viviendo en el mismo apartamento.
items.en: We're still living in the same apartment.
items.why: Nosotros → seguimos (no stem change in the nosotros form).

items.q: Tengo que llamar a mi hermana. Voy a ___ esta noche.
items.en: I have to call my sister. I'm going to call her tonight.
items.why: After 'voy a' the pronoun attaches to the infinitive: llamarla (no accent needed).

items.q: ¿El informe? Estoy ___ ahora mismo.
items.en: The report? I'm writing it right now.
items.why: Pronoun attached to the gerund, with an accent to keep the stress: escribiéndolo.

items.q: Si tienes una pregunta, ___.
items.en: If you have a question, tell me.
items.why: Affirmative tú command + attached pronoun: dime.

items.q: ¿La tarea? No ___ hoy.
items.en: The homework? I can't finish it today.
items.why: Both positions are correct: la puedo terminar = puedo terminarla.

items.en: I see her every day.
items.a: La veo todos los días.
alt: Todos los días la veo.

items.en: My brother sent me a message yesterday.
items.a: Mi hermano me mandó un mensaje ayer.
alt: Ayer mi hermano me mandó un mensaje.
Mi hermano ayer me mandó un mensaje.
Ayer me mandó un mensaje mi hermano.
Mi hermano me mandó ayer un mensaje.
Me mandó un mensaje mi hermano ayer.
Ayer me mandó mi hermano un mensaje.

items.en: I already gave it (the book) to her.
items.a: Ya se lo di.
alt: Se lo di ya.

items.en: Can you lend it (the car) to me? (to a friend)
items.a: ¿Me lo puedes prestar?

items.en: I'm going to call him tomorrow.
items.a: Lo voy a llamar mañana.
alt: Mañana lo voy a llamar.

items.en: She is getting dressed right now.
items.a: Ella se está vistiendo ahora mismo.
alt: Ahora mismo ella se está vistiendo.
Ella ahora mismo se está vistiendo.

items.en: I get up at six every day.
items.a: Me levanto a las seis todos los días.
alt: Todos los días me levanto a las seis.

items.en: My dad is still working at the factory.
items.a: Mi papá sigue trabajando en la fábrica.

items.en: What are you doing in the kitchen? (to a friend)
items.a: ¿Qué estás haciendo en la cocina?
alt: ¿En la cocina qué estás haciendo?

items.en: I'm writing it (the email) right now.
items.a: Lo estoy escribiendo ahora mismo.
alt: Ahora mismo lo estoy escribiendo.

items.en: Please tell me the truth. (to a friend)
items.a: Por favor, dime la verdad.
alt: Dime la verdad, por favor.

items.en: I took a shower and then I got dressed.
items.a: Me bañé y luego me vestí.

items.en: Did you give the money to your sister? (to a friend)
items.a: ¿Le diste el dinero a tu hermana?
alt: ¿Le diste a tu hermana el dinero?

items.en: The bank keeps calling me.
items.a: Me siguen llamando del banco.
alt: Del banco me siguen llamando.

items.en: We're going to give them the news tomorrow.
items.a: Les vamos a dar la noticia mañana.
alt: Mañana les vamos a dar la noticia.

items.en: My kids are sleeping.
items.a: Mis hijos están durmiendo.
alt: Están durmiendo mis hijos.

opts: I gave it to my brother.
My brother gave it to me.

I'm giving it to my brother.

items.say: Me estoy vistiendo.
Sigue lloviendo.
¿Me puedes ayudar?

opts: We got up late this morning.
We go to bed late every night.
They went to bed late last night.
We went to bed late last night.

opts: I'm going to send it to you tonight.
You're going to send it to me tonight.
