turns.en: I drive a truck. When can I drive again?

opts: Mañana mismo puede manejar el camión.
Depende del procedimiento y del tipo de licencia. No maneje hasta que su médico le diga que puede.
No maneja hasta que su médico le dice.
turns.why: Driving rules depend on the procedure and on commercial licensing; keep it generic. *Hasta que* + subjunctive *diga*.

turns.es: Pero necesito trabajar. ¿Qué haría usted en mi lugar?
turns.en: But I need to work. What would you do in my place?

opts: Yo en su lugar, hablé con mi jefe.
Yo en tu lugar, hablaría con mi jefe.
Yo en su lugar, hablaría con mi jefe sobre un trabajo más ligero por un tiempo.
turns.why: Advice with the conditional (*hablaría*) and usted (*su lugar*).

turns.es: Bueno, tiene razón.
turns.en: Well, you're right.

turns.es: Doctor, estoy muy preocupada. ¿De verdad salió todo bien?
turns.en: Doctor, I'm very worried. Did everything really go well?

opts: Entiendo que esté preocupada. Sí, el procedimiento salió bien y él está descansando.
Usted no debería preocuparse nunca por nada.
turns.why: Acknowledge the emotion, then answer the question in the past: *salió bien*.

turns.es: ¿Y en la casa? ¿Qué tengo que vigilar?
turns.en: And at home? What do I need to watch for?

opts: Nada; ya no hay ningún riesgo.
Si a él le sangra la ingle, apriete fuerte encima y llame al 911. Si él tiene dolor de pecho, falta de aire, se desmaya o se le cae un lado de la cara, también llame al 911.
Si le sangraba la ingle, llamaba al 911.
turns.why: Practical warning signs for the family. Option 3 uses the imperfect (habitual past), not an instruction.

turns.es: Perdón, habla muy rápido. ¿Me lo puede repetir?
turns.en: Sorry, you're speaking very fast. Can you repeat it?

opts: Claro, perdón. Se lo repito más despacio y también se lo damos por escrito.
turns.why: Repeat slowly and give written instructions; *se lo* = it to you (usted).

roleplay.title: Discharge after AF ablation
roleplay.setup: You are the electrophysiologist discharging Sra. Gutiérrez the day after an atrial fibrillation ablation through the groin. Give groin care instructions, warning signs, medication and follow-up plans, and check understanding.
roleplay.persona: You are Teresa Gutiérrez, 58, from Jalisco, Mexico, who works cleaning offices in Chicago. You had a pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation yesterday via the right groin. You feel tired and have a small bruise in the right groin, no bleeding, no chest pain. You take a blood thinner and think you can stop it now that the ablation is done — say this only if asked about medicines. You want to know when you can shower, go back to work (your job involves lifting trash bags and mopping), and swim with your grandchildren. Use everyday Mexican Spanish with usted to the doctor; use present, preterite, and some conditional (¿podría…?, ¿qué pasaría si…?). If the doctor speaks too fast, say «Perdón, ¿me lo puede repetir más despacio?». At the end, if asked to teach back, repeat the warning signs with one small mistake the doctor should correct (say you would wait until the next day if the groin bled a lot).
roleplay.opening: Buenos días, doctor. Ya me quiero ir a mi casa. ¿Qué tengo que hacer?
goals: Explain groin care: showering vs no tub or pool for a few days, no heavy lifting or straining for a few days
Explain what to do if the groin bleeds (press hard, call 911) and the other emergency signs
Find out that she plans to stop her blood thinner and tell her to keep taking it unless her doctor tells her otherwise
Give generic return-to-work and follow-up plans without specific numbers
Use teach-back and correct her mistake about groin bleeding

roleplay.title: Phone follow-up after a pacemaker
roleplay.setup: You are calling Sr. Ortiz a few days after his new pacemaker to check on him. Ask how he has been feeling, check the wound, review arm restrictions and remote monitoring, and decide what he needs to do.
roleplay.persona: You are Ernesto Ortiz, 76, from El Salvador, retired gardener, living with your daughter. You got a pacemaker a few days ago for a slow heart rhythm with dizzy spells. You feel less dizzy. The wound under your left collarbone has been a little red and warm since yesterday; no fever, no pus — reveal this only if the doctor asks specifically about the wound. You have been lifting your left arm to hang laundry above your head — reveal only if asked how you are using your arm. You plugged in the home monitor but are not sure it works. Speak simple Central American Spanish with usted to the doctor, sometimes say «¿mande?» or «perdón, ¿cómo dijo?». Use present, preterite and present perfect. Agree to come to the clinic if the doctor asks.
roleplay.opening: ¿Bueno? Sí, habla Ernesto Ortiz.
goals: Introduce yourself and ask how he has felt since the procedure (present perfect, usted)
Ask specifically about the wound and find out it is red and warm, and ask about fever and drainage
Find out he has been raising his left arm and explain the arm restriction
Explain remote monitoring and how the clinic will check that the monitor is working
Ask him to come to the clinic to have the wound checked and review when to call 911
